Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

ecolongr 0.2.1

  • el_rrarefy(), el_drarefy() and el_rarefy() have a default depth, the smallest sample total, so el_rrarefy(x) gives every sample the same depth without dropping any. Samples with a total below depth are now dropped, with a warning that names them, and it is an error if none is left. Before, el_rrarefy() returned them unchanged and el_drarefy() and el_rarefy() used their total as the depth, as vegan does, which gave values that were not at a common depth. With check = FALSE the latter two drop silently.

ecolongr 0.2.0

Alpha diversity: richness, diversity indices and rarefaction, tested against vegan.

  • New el_diversity() and el_specnumber(), the counterparts of vegan::diversity() (Shannon, Simpson and inverse Simpson, with base) and vegan::specnumber(): one value per sample, as a named vector. They are lazy, and only the per-sample result is read into R. On a table of 10.9M rows, 2,000 samples and 30,000 taxa, el_diversity() added 37 MB of peak memory with 4 threads and 217 MB with 12, in 0.2-0.3 s. A sample with no non-zero row is absent from the result, where vegan gives an all-zero row Shannon 0, Simpson 1, inverse Simpson Inf and richness 0. groups, MARGIN, equalize.groups and the other alpha-diversity functions are not implemented.

  • New el_drarefy() and el_rarefy(), the counterparts of vegan::drarefy() and vegan::rarefy(): the expected presence of each taxon, and the expected richness of each sample, in a subsample of a common depth. They equal vegan’s results and need no random numbers. el_rarefy() has no se and takes one depth.

  • New el_rrarefy(), the counterpart of vegan::rrarefy(): a random subsample of each sample to a common depth. It draws from the same distribution as vegan but not the same random numbers, so a seed does not give vegan’s result; the tests compare means and variances over many replicates with vegan and with the exact values. The table is read into R.

  • New el_frequency_counts(): for each sample, how many taxa were seen exactly once, twice and so on. It is the input of richness estimators that count the unseen taxa, such as the breakaway package, and stays lazy.

  • The check of el_decostand(), el_drarefy(), el_rarefy(), el_diversity() and el_specnumber() now also stops on NaN and Inf quantities, which it let through before.

  • Every function has examples in its help page, run on the table bundled in the package. The README is organised by application area (alpha diversity, beta diversity and ordination), the comparison with mia is removed, and the list of differences from vegan is a new vignette. There is a package website, built by pkgdown from the main branch.

ecolongr 0.1.1

  • Fixed el_vegdist() giving wrong distances, differing between runs, when threads was above 1 and the table had more than about 120,000 rows. DuckDB wrote the table sorted by taxon in parallel without keeping the order, so a taxon could be split in two and the pairs between its halves were lost. All methods were affected; el_rda() was not, because it does not depend on the order. The sorted table is now checked as it is read, so a wrong order is an error and not a wrong result.
  • The README compares the time and memory of el_vegdist() with vegan and mia, and DESIGN.md is brought up to date.

ecolongr 0.1.0

First version, for feedback.

  • el_vegdist() computes bray, jaccard, euclidean, manhattan, canberra, aitchison and robust.aitchison dissimilarities from a long table without zeros, without building the taxa by samples matrix. The result is a dist and agrees with vegan::vegdist() to about 1e-10.
  • el_decostand() makes total, hellinger, log, pa and rclr standardisations as a lazy long table. clr is computed from the counts inside el_vegdist(method = "aitchison") and el_rda(transform = "clr"), because it makes every cell non-zero.
  • el_rda() returns an unconstrained PCA of the table, of its clr or of its completed robust clr, with the first k axes, as a vegan rda object. scores(), eigenvals(), summary(), plot(), biplot(), envfit() and procrustes() work on it, and tot.chi gives the variance the k axes leave out.
  • el_rda() prints a message with the share of the total variance that the k axes hold and the share it leaves out. Silence it with suppressMessages() or options(ecolongr.quiet = TRUE). The documentation explains why an eigenvalue is divided by tot.chi and not by the sum of the kept eigenvalues.
  • The completion rank of the robust clr is ropt, 3 as in vegan, in el_vegdist() and el_rda().
  • pseudocount for clr is a number, "inverse_depth" (1 / the sample’s total count) or a vector named by sample.
  • A vignette follows the published LMO 16S time series from the Darwin Core archive to ordinations.
  • Not implemented: constrained rda with explanatory variables, predict() and fitted() for el_rda() results, and species scores for metaMDS() on a dist.
  • R CMD check runs in CI on Linux, macOS and Windows, with the tests and the vignette. The timings in the documentation were measured on Linux only.
